The evidence points at ledger-consumer no longer deduplicating redelivered events, though without deploy data I cannot name the change that caused it.", "diagnosis": {"hypothesis": "ledger-consumer has stopped deduplicating provider events by event_id, so each webhook the provider redelivers is booked again.

The provider legitimately resent several webhooks. The receiver queued each delivery as a new Kafka message, which is expected: for example, evt_000308 sits at offsets 100, 101 and 103. Both consumers read every copy. payment-confirmer recognised the repeats (already_confirmed and refund_already_confirmed account for most of its outcomes). ledger-consumer posted nearly all of them instead of returning already_processed.

The result is 7 events posted 2 or 3 times: 6 duplicated payment.succeeded events push the ledger above the provider, and a duplicated refund.succeeded pushes pay_000217 below it. The net is +$493.23. The ledger stays balanced because each duplicate is a complete double entry. No WARN or ERROR lines appear, so the ledger-consumer is skipping its dedup check silently rather than failing at it, for example because a handler change no longer checks.

The likely trigger is a recent ledger-consumer deploy, such as a changed LEDGER_HANDLER. I could not confirm it: recent_deploys and service_health both failed because Docker did not answer. That Docker outage is a separate problem to look into.", "evidence": [{"call_id": "c1", "shows": "The alert is real. 7 events were posted 2–3 times (evt_000308 three times), the ledger is $493.23 above the provider, and it is still balanced. Our payments and refunds agree with the provider, so the error is only in the ledger postings."}, {"call_id": "c3", "shows": "ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000308 three times, from offsets 100, 101 and 103, each with a different trace id. It did not skip any of the copies."}, {"call_id": "c4", "shows": "webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times. The provider redelivered it, so the duplicates on the topic are expected input."}, {"call_id": "c5", "shows": "Over the last 10 minutes, ledger: posted ≈446, already_processed ≈15. payment-confirmer: mostly already_confirmed ≈394 and refund_already_confirmed ≈39, with only ≈11 confirmed. On the same stream, the confirmer deduplicates and the ledger does not."}, {"call_id": "c8", "shows": "ledger-consumer logged no WARN or ERROR lines in the last hour, so its dedup is being skipped silently rather than failing loudly."}, {"call_id": "c6", "shows": "recent_deploys failed (Docker did not answer), so a ledger-consumer deploy cannot be confirmed. c2 and c7 failed the same way."}], "confidence": 0.6, "proposed_fix": {"kind": "rollback", "target": "ledger-consumer", "summary": "Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings before its latest deploy, which likely changed LEDGER_HANDLER to one without event_id dedup.

Before approving, confirm the deploy history once Docker responds; the rollback action refuses if the log holds no ledger-consumer deploy to undo.

Afterwards, repair the data: reverse the extra ledger transactions so that each event keeps one posting. The extras for the first five events are 255, 266, 272, 273 and 297. evt_000298 and two postings of evt_000308 also need reversing; their transaction ids are listed in the full money-check evidence. Then re-run the money check."}, "blast_radius": "ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated. Kafka lag builds briefly and then drains, and payment confirmations are not affected. If the cause is not the deploy, the rollback does not stop the duplicates. The rollback does not fix the extra postings already booked; they need the separate data repair. Docker is currently unresponsive, so the rollback may also fail until Docker recovers.", "rollback_plan": "Redeploy ledger-consumer with the settings it ran just before the rollback, as the deploy log records them. Keep watching ledger outcome already_processed against posted, and re-run the money check."}, "fix_action": {"name": "rollback_deploy", "arguments": {"service": "ledger-consumer"}}}}
